aria: Animated recap of the Heat's 137 to 130 win over the Bucks: Giannis Antetokounmpo's driving finger roll and free throw with 3:46 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 27 points, 14 rebounds and 9 assists in his first game against Milwaukee, the top scorers, how the Heat won, and Sunday's game against Oklahoma City.
notes: Box score from the Heat's 137–130 win over the Milwaukee Bucks at Kaseya Center on Nov 18, 2026, from StatMuse's box score, line score and team stats, with game details from the Associated Press (via WSVN and CBS News Miami), the Miami Herald and the South Florida Sun-Sentinel (both via Yahoo Sports) and SB Nation's rapid recap (via Yahoo Sports). All 137 Miami points and all 130 Milwaukee points are accounted for in the StatMuse player lines, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Miami 34–23 after one, 74–48 at the half, 112–86 after three; Milwaukee won the fourth 44–25. Team stats (threes 22 of 48 to 14 of 41, free throws 35 of 44 to 30 of 39, second-chance points 20–15, points in the paint 32–56, biggest lead Miami 30, Milwaukee never led) are from StatMuse. Some outlets list Giannis with 13 rebounds; the box score, AP and the Herald give 14. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Giannis Antetokounmpo played his first game against Milwaukee, his former team, and finished one assist short of a triple-double (Miami Herald). Bam Adebayo scored 21 of his 26 in the first half (Miami Herald); Davion Mitchell's six threes were a career high (Miami Herald). Miami led by 30 with 8:21 left before the Bucks closed on a 30–9 run (AP; Miami Herald). It was Miami's sixth straight win, and the Heat haven't trailed in 127 minutes and 34 seconds (AP). Milwaukee has lost 11 straight and is 1–14, the worst 15-game start in franchise history (AP). Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and Kasparas Jakucionis, who went to Milwaukee in the Giannis trade, scored 49 combined (AP). Miami hosts Oklahoma City on Sunday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Giannis Antetokounmpo's driving finger roll with 3:46 left, plus the free throw, that made it 133–112 after Milwaukee's 12–0 run had cut a 28-point lead to 16 (clock, play and scores from StatMuse's play-by-play; the 12–0 run is also in SB Nation's recap, and the Sun-Sentinel notes Giannis returned late in the game). It is drawn as the template's short pull-up in the lane, not the exact move. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Miami Heat or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Giannis Antetokounmpo's listed 6-foot-11 and 250 pounds (StatMuse), in the Heat's home white with No. 7 (Eurohoops). No wingspan from a named source was found, so his arms are drawn at the default length. His look is the proposed one on file. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
